_comment: Payloads the oracle-leak assertion MUST stay silent on. Every one contains a construct that a naive substring implementation would abort on. A check that fires on these is a check that gets bypassed, which is the same outcome as a check that never fires. Strings prefixed 'AGENT:' load as redact.AgentText.

cases.name: english-words-in-agent-prose
cases.why: 'reason' and 'outcome' are ordinary English. An assertion that aborts here aborts on most transcripts and will be switched off.

payload.user: AGENT:The reason I chose this outcome was the data I read.

cases.name: correct-answer-in-agent-submission
cases.why: on an oracle-PASSING trace the agent's own answer IS the expected value, and PREREGISTRATION.md 4.2 requires the judge to see the submitted answer. Aborting here would abort on essentially every positive.

cases.name: expected-digits-inside-a-run-id
cases.why: run ids are timestamps. '20260803T064550-...' contains the digits of an expected value of 550. Bookkeeping is not a channel into a scorer, and redact.scorer_content keeps it out of the payload rather than exempting it from the scan.

cases.name: tool-result-containing-the-true-data
cases.why: the application returning its own correct data to the agent is the task, not a leak

cases.name: harness-text-with-no-oracle-content
cases.why: the ordinary case; the assertion must be silent on the prompt scaffold itself

payload.system: Return only a JSON object with succeeded, p_success and justification.
